# Finding and report templates

One finding, one file. Doctrine the fields encode: severity `METHODOLOGY.md §7`, dispositions `§8`,
refute-first and the verification record `§6.7`, debate `§6.8`, dedup `§6.9`, provenance Rule M1 `§5.2`,
disclosure `§15`. A field left empty is written `n/a: <reason>`, never omitted, except: severity cell,
root cause `path:line`, scenario numbers, proof (at MEDIUM and above) and dedup key are never `n/a`. A candidate that cannot fill them,
or sits at Undetermined or traced-but-unexecuted, stays a LEAD and is not filed.

## 1. Finding

```markdown
## <ID>  <title: the mechanism and its consequence, one line, no adjectives>

| field | value |
|---|---|
| id | workbook row id (private) · published bundle id F-nn (public) |
| severity | CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / INFO / Undetermined |
| impact × likelihood | I1-I5 × L1-L4 → cell; cap applied: <none / L1 key / L2 privileged mistake>; no other cap exists |
| difficulty | low / medium / high, given the preconditions hold |
| blast radius | leg / pool / fleet / treasury / LP principal |
| class | AUDIT / QA (`§1.1`) · CODE / ECON / ORACLE / GOV / OPS / SPEC / ROUTINE |
| sub-scope · hop | e.g. hooks · pool contracts |
| affected | `Contract.function` @ repo@sha · chains · addresses |
| live_today | true / false (`§7.4`: severity is at the shipping configuration either way) |
| status | OPEN / FIXED / ACCEPTED / CLOSED / REFUTED / DUPLICATE / SUBSUMED / MOOT |
| dedup key | (contract, function, state variables, invariant, fix shape) |
```

**Severity rationale.** The `§7.2` order in one line each: harm named → invariant broken (published or
inferred) → impact level and why → likelihood as the hardest precondition → cap, if any. Example shape:
"I5: LP principal on the leg is sold at par during a real depeg. L3: needs a depeg on both feeds. HIGH
before cap; no cap applies; latent, so live_today = false."

### Root cause

`path:line` (private) or `Contract.function` (public) of the defect, plus the one sentence that states the
**mechanism**, not the symptom: "<untrusted input> reaches <operation> without <guard>", or the invariant
the code fails to preserve. A symptom ("swap succeeds", "balance drops") is not a root cause. Quote the
smallest code excerpt that shows it, headed by its site.

### Preconditions

Numbered, each with its L-level and whether it holds at the shipping configuration:

1. <actor and capability> (L4 / L3 / L2 / L1)
2. <market or protocol state, with the parameter values that make it reachable>
3. <ordering or timing requirement>

### Scenario

Numbered transaction or event steps with concrete numbers at shipping parameters: amounts, prices,
parameter values, block or time deltas, and the state after each step. End with the attacker's net and the
LP / protocol loss, both in token units and in % of the affected leg's TVL. Attacker net is after every
cost the protocol charges (fees, tolls, spreads, caps) and gas. A repeated attack states whether the bound is
a stock (one-shot to a wall) or a flow (per block / per push), and why.

### Numbers

Every number the severity rests on, one row each. Severity cites the bounded formula, not one illustrative
trade. A finding whose key number is `assumed` is not filed.

| quantity | value | provenance | source | sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e.g. LP loss per episode | bps of leg L | derived / measured / assumed | derived: formula + `path:line`; measured: command + snapshot hash; assumed: why | the parameter whose change flips severity, and its flip value |

### Impact

Who loses what, bounded how. Magnitude as a number or a bounded formula evaluated at shipping parameters;
blast radius (which legs, pools, chains); contagion path if any; duration. A finding with harm stated only as
a mechanism is capped at INFO (`§6.3`). Blast radius cites code, never a design memory: a multi-asset pool
whose legs share a counter-asset has radius `pool`.

### Likelihood and difficulty

Attacker cost (capital, gas, fees, tolls, opportunity), detection by existing monitors and how fast, and
what levers stop it once detected. Likelihood is the hardest precondition; difficulty is the effort once it
holds. Do not collapse the two.

### Proof

| field | value |
|---|---|
| method | trace / PoC / measurement / simulation |
| artefact | test or script path and name (PoCs are never committed: name the regression test that replaces it) |
| command | exact command, pinned heads |
| state | fork block and state hash, or the fixture and its parameter set |
| pre-fix | output at the vulnerable code: the exploit succeeds, with the key number |
| post-fix | output at the fix: the same call reverts or the key number is bounded (once a fix exists) |
| attacked direction | every direction or path the scenario uses is exercised, not a neighbour |
| status | VERIFIED (both sides observed) / DISPROVED / ERROR / traced-but-unexecuted: <blocker> (`§6.7` runner semantics) |

A sim counts only with inputs loaded from the recorded state; the validator re-runs it on a perturbed seed.

### Remediation

The fix shape (add-require / reorder / clamp / new state / control flow / redesign) and what it could
break. Precise steps or a diff sketch; for an OPEN row, the recommended option first, alternatives after,
each with its cost and residual. A requirement on a producer-controlled field names the producer's
guarantee and the on-chain measurement that confirms it (`§9.3`).

### Fix status

| field | value |
|---|---|
| fix commit | repo@sha (must descend from the freeze head, `§11`) |
| regression test | path::name, mutant it catches (`§9.1`); run on the pre-fix code and fails there |
| differential review | LN-31 verdict on the fix diff, LN-32 variant sweep result (sites checked, variants found) |
| deployed | per chain: address, tx or block of the upgrade / config change; on-chain codehash = a reproducible build at the fix commit |
| verification | the post-deploy check: tx, call output or test against the deployed code |

### Cross-validation record

| role | count | verdict | key number reproduced | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| finders | n (blind to each other) | — | — | family, requested and served model, lens, regime, priming per pass |
| challenger(s) | 1 below HIGH, 2 at HIGH+ | TRUE / FALSE / DOWNGRADE / UPGRADE | yes / no | idem; same-family exception recorded |
| cross-cohort validator | ≥ 1 | idem | yes / no | idem |
| third reviewer | on a split | idem | | idem |
| debate | link to record | settled / design advisory + dissent entry | | |
| chair verdict | | | | |

Guards checked and search patterns tried for every absence the finding asserts, listed, not summarised.

## 2. Public and private variants

| rule | private (workbook) | public (mirror, report) |
|---|---|---|
| when | at filing | only when FIXED and deployed on every chain running the code (`§15`); held in full until then, no redacted form |
| code references | `repo/path:line` and excerpts | open repos: `path:line` survives; closed repos: `Contract.function` + verified address + explorer source link; no line numbers |
| commits | full sha links | open repos: links; closed repos: `repo@sha` text |
| off-chain internals (price source, signing tier, keys, infra) | kept | removed; replaced by the on-chain observable effect and the parity or test claim that bounds it |
| provenance | per pass, Rule M1 fields | none per finding (`§5.3`); aggregated as rates in the report |
| ids | workbook row id | bundle id F-nn only |
| PoC | path in a gitignored scratch dir, then deleted | never; the regression test name instead |
| numbers | all | all that do not depend on a private internal |

A public variant is generated from the private file, never written by hand.

## 3. Report

```markdown
# <product> security review <yyyy-mm>

## 1. Executive summary
Scope in one line; findings by severity with OPEN first; the residual-risk headline; what changed since
the last report.

## 2. Scope at pinned heads
| repo | sha | in scope | out of scope |   (both directions, `§6.1`; boilerplate marked by origin)

## 3. Method
Pointer to METHODOLOGY.md at its version; deviations from it for this review, if any; roster and effort
(rounds, cohorts, agent-passes, families, wall clock, tokens: `§13` item 8).

## 4. Coverage evidence
| entry point / hop / scenario | score | eyes required | eyes spent | families | lenses | status |
Rates: minimum over rows, share of rows at budget, negative coverage (N/A with reason, never reached)
beside positive, single-family score-5 share. The row that sets the minimum and each named deficit are
published once covered or fixed.

## 5. Findings
Open first, then by severity, then by blast radius (a LOW with fleet radius does not sort last).
One table row per bundle: id · severity · difficulty · blast radius · title · status · fix commit ·
deployed chains. Full finding bodies follow, in the public variant.
Refuted, duplicate, subsumed and moot counts published separately (`§8`).

## 6. Residual risk
The eight items of `§13`: coverage floor, single-family paths, unenforced assumptions with live
violations, designed and accepted risks with their bounds, formal reach, open findings, corrections
register, effort.

## 7. Limits
`§14` as it applies to this scope, in the strongest form.
```

## 4. Worked example

The worked example lives in the private workbook and publishes with its bundle under the disclosure rule
(`METHODOLOGY.md §15`). Until it does, this template has no published worked example.
